files.scenario_summary: Ten close-retry scenarios check the ordinary close result, retry ownership, transport-owned errors, shared pending attempts, concurrent observers, re-entry, repeated failures and recovery, and the already-closed peer case. The 1..1000 failure loop is followed by a recovery attempt. Concurrent case uses 8 worker threads for 64 submitted caller tasks, each producing 128 observations (8,192 total), gates the held attempt, and verifies observer changes do not mutate shared results.

Shutdown is requested from the dial visitor while publication is in progress. The dial failure, absence of late publication, physical UDP parent close/unregistration, and owned group completion are asserted.

Repeated shutdown is started while the first child operation is held. Assertions check the UDP parent remains open until the child operation settles, and check the resulting close outcome and terminal state.
Two boolean input modes exercise a secondary UDP-parent close failure. The test asserts the surfaced failure identity, child/parent close state, and termination of the owned group.
The UDP parent close path is entered after its event loop is terminated. Assertions cover future settlement, closed/unregistered parent state, and group/loop terminal state.
Two boolean input modes exercise a UDP-parent close failure that is not added as a suppressed failure. The test asserts the surfaced outcome, resource close state, and owned-group termination.
Two boolean input modes call shutdown repeatedly after UDP-parent close failure. Assertions check failure identity across calls, closure of owned resources, and group termination.
One listener close failure is combined with repeated TCP shutdown. Eight accepted roots are created; assertions check all listeners and accepted roots close and worker threads terminate.

Shutdown is requested while a bind is queued. The dial remains pending at the held step, then fails before handshake/connection publication; assertions check the active connection count and server listener state.

Eight rounds of sixteen child dials (128 total) exercise child close and UDP parent release during continued transport use. Assertions check port/resource release, active connection counts, and that the client group and server listener remain usable.
Close occurs while listener certificate preparation is held. Assertions check the listen request fails and no listener or listen address is published.

Transport shutdown is attempted with a live child after its loop rejects dispatch. Assertions cover child/parent future settlement, physical close state, loop/group termination, and independent server state.

Four outbound children and four client UDP parents each have a distinct close failure. Assertions check primary failure identity, reachability of all eight failure objects through causes/suppressed failures, one close request per resource, and client/server terminal-state ownership.
A released UDP parent is followed by a rejected loop dispatch. Assertions check the earlier successful result remains successful and inspect parent/loop/group state after transport shutdown.
A connection close rejection is recorded before loop termination. First and repeated transport shutdown assert that the earlier rejection remains the reported failure and check resource/group states.
A failed handshake releases the bound UDP port while the transport remains usable. Assertions check the handshake error, subsequent usability, and physical port release/rebind.
Shutdown is requested during a held handshake. Assertions check the in-flight dial does not publish, then fails and releases the bound UDP port while preserving the server listener.

Shutdown starts while an ordinary child close has already physically removed the child. Assertions check shutdown waits on that close outcome, preserves failure identity, and reaches the expected parent state.
An ordinary close already in progress is held while whole-transport shutdown begins. Assertions check shutdown adopts the outstanding child/parent close barrier and does not finish prematurely.

A failed connection setup does not report its failure before the UDP port is physically released. The held close keeps the port bound while the operation is pending; release precedes the expected dial failure.
A failed datagram setup is held at physical UDP-parent close. Assertions check the dial remains pending while the port is bound and reports the expected failure only after release/rebind.

A close request from the callback path meets a failed physical parent close. Assertions check the dial remains pending until the held close settles, then reports the same failure and releases the port.
A callback requests close while child and parent release are pending. Assertions check the dial remains pending and the real connection/parent stay open until their close steps complete.

The test derives the active loop count, creates loopCount+1 failed dials, and chooses two channels with the same EventLoop object. It holds both UDP-parent close completions, asserts both dials remain pending and both ports remain bound, then releases and checks the visitor failures, port rebinds, and one close request per parent.

Two ownership cases check network and connection shutdown share one physical parent close: the pending case checks both owners wait on the same close; the failed case checks all owners receive the failed close without another physical request.
One listener close fails while other listeners and eight accepted roots still close. Assertions cover close failure identity, all listener/root terminal states, and worker-group termination.

Seven input modes (listener, connection, listener-throw, listener-deferred, caller-cancel, caller-complete, success) exercise transport shutdown and assert the expected failure identity, closure, and termination of every acceptor thread.
Closing an outbound child does not discard the transport owner of its UDP parents. Assertions check child close and then parent/group shutdown ownership and terminal state.

Six input modes (listener, listener-throw, listener-deferred, caller-cancel, caller-complete, success) exercise QUIC transport close and assert the expected outcome and termination of every worker thread.

One outbound close failure is combined with four outbound connections and their UDP parents. Assertions check the exact failure outcome, all child/parent closure, client group termination, and continued server-side listener ownership. A diagnostic println at line 115 is not the evidence; explicit assertions follow at lines 124–139.
Two boolean input modes exercise failed UDP-parent close while the transport-owned group is shut down. Assertions cover the surfaced failure, closed state, and group termination.
A connection-handler close request is held at physical UDP-parent release. Assertions check the dial remains pending while the port is bound, then check the post-release dial outcome and port rebind.
A rejected close leaves the UDP parent open. Assertions check the rejection identity and that the dial does not wait for selector-driven release while the parent remains open.
A successful closed dial waits for the UDP port to be physically released. Assertions check pending state and bound port before release, then failure/rebind after release.
A successful QUIC dial result is withheld until the UDP port is physically released. Assertions check pending state, physical release/rebind, and the final visitor result.

special_scenario_inventory.evidence: F93jQuicSameLoopReleaseTest.kt:34-130. It selects channels with identical EventLoop identity (assertSame at line 72), holds both parent close completions, checks pending dial futures and bound ports before releasing the gates (lines 94-100), then checks failures, port rebinds and one close request per parent (lines 72-84). No output-only evidence is used.

ConnectionCloseRetryTest.kt:96-118 and :281-305. Reentrant operation is checked as still pending at lines 104 and 292; result/failure identity and physical close request count are asserted at lines 110-112 and 302-303.

The close/shutdown tests assert futures complete and inspect channel isOpen/isRegistered, event-loop/group isShuttingDown/isTerminated, thread liveness, parent/child state, or listener counts. Representative assertion sites: F93bQuicTerminatedLoopTest.kt:73-85; F93cQuicLiveChildRejectedLoopTest.kt:82-99; F93cQuicMultipleCloseFailuresTest.kt:179-195; QuicTransportFailedCloseTest.kt:96-101; QuicTransportFailedConnectionSetTest.kt:124-139; PlainNettyTransportFailedCloseTest.kt:107-114.

F93cQuicMultipleCloseFailuresTest.kt:130, 134, 138, 143, 152, 166, 173, 176 and 179-195 checks primary identity, the eight distinct reachable failures, one close request per child/parent, and resource state. F93cQuicTerminationFailureRetentionTest.kt:75, 81, 91 and 98-115 checks the earlier rejection remains after first and repeated shutdown. ConnectionCloseRetryTest.kt:264, 267-274 checks the 1,000 failure loop and recovery. These outcomes are assertions, not diagnostic output.

F93bQuicDialPublicationTest.kt:40-50 checks failed dial and no connection publication; F93cQuicBindShutdownTest.kt:45-52 checks no handshake/connection publication; F93cQuicListenShutdownTest.kt:43-47 checks no listener/address publication; F93dQuicHandshakeShutdownTest.kt:57-67 checks no connection publication; F93jCallbackPendingChildReleaseTest.kt:49-57 checks pending state around child/parent close; F93jCallbackFailedParentReleaseTest.kt:58, 61, 64, 69-70 checks bound-port pending state followed by the reported close failure identity. All use assertions.

QuicTransportFailedConnectionSetTest.kt:115 prints diagnostic state. That same test then asserts UDP-parent futures and resource/group state at lines 124-139. The other 34 test files have no print/stacktrace/logger sites detected.
